extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, editors, and journal staff of biomedical/medical journals
extracted.subtask_description: Official ICMJE recommendations for the conduct, reporting, editing, and publication of scholarly work in medical journals, including authorship criteria, peer‑review responsibilities, publication ethics, and guidance on use/acknowledgement of AI tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship — based on four criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: In the section on 'Who is an Author' (Section II.A.2), the ICMJE recommends that authorship be based on 4 criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement notes that authorship should meet four ICMJE criteria (full criteria text is in the ICMJE Recommendations PDF). An annotated PDF is available to identify changes; the official full Recommendations PDF is downloadable from icmje.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criterion #2 — wording: 'Drafting or reviewing critically'
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion #2 was revised from 'Drafting the work or revising it critically for important intellectual content' to 'Drafting the work or reviewing it critically for important intellectual content'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICMJE changed the wording because some readers interpreted 'revising' to require making changes to earlier manuscript versions to qualify for authorship. The revised wording clarifies that all authors must at minimum review the manuscript critically for important intellectual content AND have the opportunity to make changes if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of work assisted by AI
rubrics_metrics.description: ICMJE added a new subsection (II.A.4) and revised other sections (II.C.3, IV.A.3.g) to provide guidance on how work conducted with the assistance of AI technology (including ChatGPT and similar tools) should and should not be acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement signals new requirements/guidance about disclosure/acknowledgement of AI assistance by authors and related updates elsewhere in the Recommendations. For full text and specific disclosure language, consult the updated ICMJE Recommendations PDF/annotated PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewers' responsibilities (Section II.C.3) — revised
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibilities of peer reviewers in the submission and peer-review process have been revised (Section II.C.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The updates include revised language about reviewers' responsibilities; the announcement also links these updates to AI-related guidance. Consult the updated Recommendations for detailed reviewer responsibilities and any new expectations (e.g., regarding use or detection of AI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/handling of duplicate publication (Section III.D.2) — revised
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICMJE revised what is considered duplicate publication (Section III.D.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement notes a revision to the duplicate-publication standard; see the full Recommendations for the precise updated definition and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for sex and gender (Section IV.A.2) — updated
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting guidelines related to sex and gender have been revised (Section IV.A.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The update addresses how sex and gender should be reported in manuscripts to improve clarity and inclusiveness; refer to the updated Recommendations for specific expectations and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI by authors (Section V.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Recommendations include a section on use of AI by authors (Section V.A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The News announcement highlights added/revised guidance on acknowledging AI assistance in authoring. For concrete rules on permitted/forbidden AI uses and required disclosures, see the updated Recommendations PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI by reviewers (Section V.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Recommendations include a section on use of AI by reviewers (Section V.B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement indicates guidance for reviewers who may use AI tools in the review process; consult the full Recommendations for specifics on acceptable practices and disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' role in ensuring responsible use of AI (Section V.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Recommendations include guidance on editors' responsibilities to ensure responsible use of AI in publishing (Section V.C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are given guidance on policy, oversight, and implementation relating to AI-assisted work; see the updated Recommendations for operational details and policy language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive language throughout
rubrics_metrics.description: The Recommendations include other revisions to assure more inclusive language throughout the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The update mentions broad revisions to wording to improve inclusivity; specific examples and replacement language appear in the full updated Recommendations/annotated PDF.
